rule: JSON projection of the YAML registry for the DB ingest and the staging resolver; regenerated by pipeline/select_obr_costings_claims.py and checked against the YAML by tests

measures.obr_description: PA and HRT freezes
measures.notes: Reverses the certified freezes using Table 3.19's published with-indexation PA and gross HRT path. The PE HRT parameter is a taxable band width, so each value is published gross HRT minus published PA. The Table 3.17 line bundles several announcement events; no single event decomposition is asserted.

measures.obr_description: Additional rate threshold: reduction
measures.notes: Reverses £125,140 to the previous £150,000 threshold. Both the main and dividend threshold paths are set because PE-UK 2.89.2 stores them separately.

measures.obr_description: NICs: rise in primary threshold
measures.notes: Reverses to Table 3.19's published indexed annual primary-threshold path, divided by 52 because the installed PE parameter is weekly. Employer and Class 4 aggregates remain in the required broad NICs head even when their direct deltas are zero. The certified PT starts uprating in 2028, so the published Table 3.19 counterfactual can fall below that baseline in outer years; those construction-direction changes are retained and annotated rather than treated as an assumption-matched reversal.

measures.obr_description: Class 2 NICs: threshold rise
measures.notes: The Class 2 parameters exist, but PE-UK does not retain the required indexed counterfactual path for this 3.17 re-estimate. Class 2 is also outside the lane brief's prescribed broad NICs aggregate. No mechanics are invented.

measures.obr_description: Class 1 NICs: threshold freezes
measures.notes: Uses Table 3.19's indexed UEL/UPL path (UEL divided by 52). The 3.17 plural line does not disclose a secondary-threshold counterfactual, so that component is missing and the construction is partial.

measures.obr_description: Autumn Statement 2023 NICs reduction
measures.notes: Reverses the Class 1 2p and Class 4 1p legs while retaining the later Spring Budget 2024 cuts. The Table 3.17 aggregate also includes Class 2 abolition; that leg is omitted because its counterfactual is not stored and Class 2 is outside the prescribed NICs head.

measures.obr_description: Spring Budget 2024 NICs reduction
measures.notes: Reverses the two 2 percentage-point rate legs represented by the 3.17 line. PE annual processing samples the April rates for calendar 2024.

measures.obr_description: Autumn Budget 2024 employer NICs rise
measures.notes: Reverses the employer rate and weekly secondary threshold. PE-UK lacks Employment Allowance and firm-level eligibility mechanics, which are part of the OBR package, so this is partial.

measures.obr_description: National Insurance contributions (NICs): 2p cut to the main rate of Class 1 employee NICs from January 2024
measures.notes: The Class 1 rate lever is direct. PE static head mappings do not model the OBR's corporation-tax, capital-gains-tax, departmental-spending, or Scottish block-grant channels. Welfare inside cap is represented only by universal_credit, not the full OBR welfare-head scope.

measures.obr_description: National Insurance contributions (NICs): 1p cut to the main rate of Class 4 self-employed NICs from April 2024
measures.notes: Direct Class 4 rate reversal. Welfare inside cap is represented only by universal_credit, and non-microsimulation OBR heads remain unmapped.

measures.obr_description: National Insurance contributions (NICs): abolish Class 2 self-employed NICs liability from April 2024
measures.notes: PE's Class 2 flat-rate path records zero after abolition but does not store an indexed 2024+ counterfactual, and Class 2 is outside the lane's prescribed NICs aggregate. No reversal value is guessed.

measures.obr_description: National Insurance contributions (NICs): 2 percentage point cut to the main rate of Class 1 employee NICs from 6 April 2024
measures.notes: Direct Class 1 rate reversal; PE calendar 2024 proxies FY 2024-25. Welfare inside cap is represented only by universal_credit, not the full OBR welfare-head scope, and the named non-microsimulation heads are omitted.

measures.obr_description: National Insurance contributions (NICs): 2 percentage point cut to the main rate of Class 4 self-employed NICs from 6 April 2024
measures.notes: Direct Class 4 rate reversal; PE calendar 2024 proxies FY 2024-25. Welfare inside cap is represented only by universal_credit, not the full OBR welfare-head scope, and the named non-microsimulation heads are omitted.

measures.obr_description: High Income Child Benefit Charge: increase income threshold to £60,000 and taper range to £60,000 to £80,000 from 6 April 2024
measures.notes: The HICBC tax-charge formula and thresholds are direct. child_benefit is a PROVISIONAL PE head mapping for the OBR "Welfare inside cap" head. The matched harvest row identifies neither the programme nor a mechanism. PE's would_claim_child_benefit is fixed in this static run, so the PE child_benefit delta is zero.

measures.obr_description: Employer National Insurance contributions: Increase rate by 1.2 ppts to 15%, cut the Secondary Threshold to £5,000 until 5 April 2028 and uprate with CPI thereafter, increase Employment Allowance to £10,500, remove the £100,000 Employment Allowance eligibility threshold
measures.notes: PE represents the employer rate and weekly secondary threshold (£96 × 52 = £4,992 in the installed model). It has no Employment Allowance or firm entity, so the allowance increase and £100,000 test removal are missing. policyengine_uk/parameters/gov/contrib/policyengine/employer_ni/employee_incidence.yaml sets gov.contrib.policyengine.employer_ni.employee_incidence to 1, and policyengine_uk/variables/contrib/policyengine/employer_ni/employer_ni_fixed_employer_cost_change.py adjusts wages holding employer cost fixed. The resulting wage change moves employee-side Income Tax and NICs, which is why the PE Income-tax head is non-zero.

measures.obr_description: Abolition of non-domicile tax status and introduction of a residence-based regime: remove the 50% discount on foreign income in 2025/26; apply inheritance tax; set Capital Gains Tax rebasing date at 5 April 2017; and extend the Temporary Repatriation Facility from two to three years
measures.notes: The residence history, foreign-income discount, CGT rebasing, IHT, and Temporary Repatriation Facility package is not a plain PE-UK parameter reform in this version.

measures.obr_description: Increased collection of tax due supported by investment in 5,000 additional HMRC compliance staff
measures.notes: Compliance staffing and collection yield are not microsimulation parameters.

measures.obr_description: Dividend Income: Increase tax rates on dividend income by 2ppts at the ordinary and upper rate from 6 April 2026
measures.notes: Reverses the certified ordinary/basic and upper/higher dividend rates to 8.75% and 33.75%; the additional rate was not changed by this measure. PE maps Income Tax directly and retains the required broad NICs aggregate, but cross-tax, departmental-spending, and block-grant heads are outside this static construction.

measures.obr_description: Property Income: Introduce separate tax rates for property income at 22% for the property basic rate, 42% for the property higher rate and 47% for the property additional rate, from 6 April 2027
measures.notes: Reverses the three certified property-income rates to 20%, 40%, and 45%. PE maps the direct Income Tax liability; the OBR also allocates effects to taxes and the Scottish block grant that this construction does not model.

measures.obr_description: Savings Income: Increase tax rates on savings income by 2ppts at the basic, higher and additional rate from 6 April 2027 and maintain the Starting Rate of Savings limit at £5000 from April 2026 to April 2031
measures.notes: Reverses the three certified savings-income rates to 20%, 40%, and 45%. The same OBR measure freezes the Starting Rate for Savings limit at £5,000, but PE's parameter is constant at £5,000 since 2010 and carries no no-measure uprating path; that component is omitted.

measures.obr_description: Salary Sacrifice: Limit the value of salary sacrificed pension contributions that can receive employee and employer NICs relief to £2,000 per year from 6 April 2029
measures.notes: PE's exact pre-policy cap is infinity, which standard JSON cannot retain in the required run artifact. This construction uses a finite 1e100 cap, above any modeled contribution, and sets the model's fixed 0.16% broad-base pay-haircut response to zero; code inspection verifies that this leaves salary sacrifice uncapped on the modeled data. The certified formula otherwise embeds that behavioural incidence assumption, and the OBR scores small pre-2029 effects that the direct PE lever cannot produce.

measures.obr_description: Winter Fuel Payment: Target to pensioners with taxable income below or equal to £35,000 from Winter 2025
measures.notes: Turns off the certified £35,000 England-and-Wales income passport while retaining the 2024 means-tested-benefit requirement. PE computes gross winter_fuel_allowance spending and Income Tax (expected to have no direct WFP recovery change); its formula uses income below £35,000 rather than the OBR description's below-or-equal wording and returns zero in Scotland.

measures.obr_description: Universal Credit: Changes to the standard allowance and health element to protect existing claimants and new health element claimants who meet the Severe Conditions Criteria from April 2026
measures.notes: PE's scenario layer randomly labels post-2025 claimants using hard-coded shares, does not test a Severe Conditions Criteria variable, and does not expose the full protection as a plain parameter dictionary. The available rebalancing uplift parameter is not referenced by a formula. No scalar proxy or inside/outside-cap allocation is assumed.

measures.obr_description: Personal Tax: Maintain the personal income tax and equivalent national insurance thresholds at current levels for a further three years until April 2031
measures.notes: Reverses the PA/main/dividend HRT extension using the installed parameters' documented CPI uprating indices. The certified bundle already resumes uprating PT/UEL from 2028 and Class 4 limits from 2027, so it does not consistently encode the equivalent-NI freeze; this construction is partial and makes no NI threshold override.

measures.obr_description: National Insurance: Maintain the secondary threshold for employer contributions at current level for a further three years until April 2031
measures.notes: Counterfactual weekly values apply the installed parameter's documented OBR-CPI uprating to £96 from 2028. Exact source rounding and non-microsimulation heads are not assumption-matched, so this is partial.

measures.obr_description: Universal Credit Child Element: Remove the two child limit from April 2026, taking 450,000 children out of poverty
measures.notes: Reverses the UC child-element limit from infinity to two. The OBR also reports a Welfare outside cap row, but the harvest does not identify its program composition; CTC or devolved-offset mechanics are not assumed.
